claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
For NLBs, ingress traffic to the load balancer must be opened explicitly, but not for ALBs.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
The Pulumi AWS registry has API docs for the aws.ec2 LaunchTemplate resource at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
In AWSx, passing the load balancer's target group in the task definition's `portMappings` makes AWSx populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration automatically.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw aws.ecs requires manual security group management.
The awsx-load-balanced-fargate-nginx example exports a stack output named `url`, used by `pulumi stack output url`.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive for ECS than NLBs: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
By default, an AWSx load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
AWSx load balancers accept a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs) for explicit subnets.
NLB listeners support protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC; ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP.
AWS docs page rule-action-types.html contains #fixed-response-actions and #redirect-actions anchors.
AWS documentation page listener-rules.html exists for listener rules.
ELB `deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds with a default of 300.
ELB `slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable, disabled by default.
Target group stickiness is supported for ALBs only.
Target group `targetType` values are instance, ip, lambda, and alb; default is instance; IPs must be in the VPC private range, RFC 1918, or RFC 6598 (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds with a default of 30 seconds.
Health check `healthyThreshold` range is 2–10 with default 3.
Health check `unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10 with default 3; for NLBs it must equal healthyThreshold.
Health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
